mu_name_from: MuMain loads the orbs as gems: ZzzOpenData.cpp line 1047, `for i in 0..13: if (i + 7 != 15) AccessModel(MODEL_WING + i + 7, L"Data\\Item\\", L"Gem", i + 1)`, so group 12 number n is Gem{n-6}: number 11 is Gem05. openmu's 0.75 Orbs.cs puts the Orb of Summoning at 12, 11 - `CreateOrb(11, SkillNumber.SummonGoblin, ...)`. mu.db carries no group-12 rows at all, so the two sources here are the client and OpenMU and they agree.
why_this_one:
The one thing in the Budge Dragon's pool that was missed when it was counted. Shield01's note counts eleven rows at drop level 4 or under in the 0.75 table - five weapons, an apple, a shield, four pieces of armour - and the orbs were not looked at. This is the twelfth: drop level 3, and it drops from monsters.

It is also the only thing a Lorencia monster leaves for the Elf that is not a bow or a crossbow, and the first item from the wing group - which in 0.75 is wings, orbs and jewels together under group 12 - to carry a drop row.
profile_note: Not because an orb is a weapon but for the reason Potion01 gives: the profile is about the art, a small painted sheet on a made object seen close, upscaled with the drawn model held back. A 32-square sphere is that. The default material is overridden below.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Orbs.cs line 36. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call: CreateOrb(11, SkillNumber.SummonGoblin, 1, "Orb of Summoning", 3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 150, CharacterClasses.FairyElf); summonOrb.MaximumItemLevel = 5
stats.call_note: CreateOrb(number, skillNumber, height, name, dropLevel, levelRequirement, energyRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, money, characterClasses). It sets Group = 12, Width = 1, DropsFromMonsters = true and Durability = 1 itself, so those are not in the call.
stats.drop_level_note: Three, so a Budge Dragon at level 4 can afford it and a Spider at 2 cannot. `(4 - 3) / 3` is nought, so it falls plain. Written on the definition as DropsFromMonsters = true, which is a real flag here rather than an absence - the jewels in the same group say false.
stats.classes_from: CharacterClasses.FairyElf, and no requirement of any kind - the only row in the dragon's pool with nothing to lift. It teaches the Elf Summon Goblin, which is what the durability of one is: it is used once.

skill.note: What the orb teaches at +0. The plus is the skill, so this block is the base and Prize.Teaching adds the plus: SummoningOrbConsumeHandlerPlugIn teaches `baseSkillNumber + item.Level`, +0 Summon Goblin (30) to +5 Summon Bali (35), and Lala stocks +0 to +4. See docs/summoning.md.
skill.name: Summon Goblin
skill.tells: Calls a monster to fight at her side until it falls. The better the orb, the bigger what answers -- a goblin at first, Bali at the last.
skill.tells_from: What the skill DOES, which is the line the tooltip prints under its name. MU never says it -- a scroll's tooltip there is the name, the requirement and the class -- so this is ours, and it describes the spell rather than its price: the numbers behind it (damage, range, mana, element, area) are in OpenMU's Version075/SkillsInitializer.cs and in docs/mu-scrolls-and-orbs.md, and the tooltip has its own rows for what a thing costs.
skill.energy_from: OpenMU puts no requirement on the orb and checks the skill's energy at every cast (30 for the Goblin, SkillsInitializer.cs:68). MuMain checks it before the orb can be used, and for this item alone replaces the formula with a switch on the plus: 30, 60, 90, 130, 170, 210 (ZzzInfomation.cpp:798-814). This is the +0 value; the others are in Prize.Teaching, because the index carries one energy per row.

refinement_note:
This row is the one exception to Prize.TakesRefinement so far, and it is recorded rather than coded. The rule says nothing above group 11 wears a plus, which is right for every other orb, jewel and wing - and OpenMU gives this one `MaximumItemLevel = 5`, because the summon orb's level picks what it summons: a Goblin at +0 and a stronger monster at each plus above it. Nothing in Lorencia is big enough to give it a level - the Skeleton Warrior at 19 would make `(19 - 3) / 3` = 5 and cap there, but it drops nothing above its own pool - so the rule holds until something does. When it stops holding, the fix is a per-row maximum on Prize rather than a widening of the group test.

And the plus is what it teaches: see the skill block, and Prize.Teaching.
sheet_from: Data/Item/pearl.OZJ (32x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names pearl.jpg, and every one of the 48 triangles is on it - one sheet, one submesh.
sheet_note:
A deep blue sphere on black, mean (10, 52, 76): a paler swirl curling through the centre with three small white highlights on it, fading to near-black at the corners. It is a painted glass ball, and the highlights are painted on - which is worth knowing before a material adds its own.

32 square is the whole of what MU shipped, and the sheet is shared: every Gem model in the folder is one of a handful of pearls, so an upscale here is an upscale for the other orbs when they come.
cutout_from: No alpha in the .OZJ, and the sheet is a sphere's skin rather than a card, so there is nothing to cut.
material_note: glass, over the weapon profile's steel. One island, the whole sphere, and it is a painted glass ball: metallic 0, roughness 0.12, no grain. Written for this item - see materials/glass.json for why ceramic, the nearest thing already there, is a glaze over clay and not the same surface. The three highlights MU painted on the sheet stay, and the material adds one real one over them.
